name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
problem: Text embeddings were evaluated on a couple of STS datasets, so field progress could not be tracked and models did not generalise across task types.
mechanism: A BENCHMARK, not a method: 8 embedding task types over 58 datasets and 112 languages, with a standard evaluation harness and a public leaderboard, used to evaluate 33 models. Its central empirical finding is that no method dominates across all tasks.
speedup_reported: Benchmarks 33 models across 8 tasks, 58 datasets and 112 languages, and establishes that no particular text embedding method dominates across all tasks - i.e. the field has not converged on a universal method. No speedup claim; this is an evaluation artifact.
notes:
Venue EACL 2023 (crossref 'Proceedings of the 17th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics'). Recorded because it changed how this field buys models: MTEB scores are the default acceptance gate for an embedding model, and its headline finding is the warning that a single benchmark score is not a reason to swap a production embedder. The hardware-relevant consequence is indirect but real - a benchmark that ranks encoders lets you trade model size against recall without running your own retrieval eval.
